_comment_family: Montserrat Regular, the static cut from the Google Fonts download of
the family (static/Montserrat-Regular.ttf, Version 9.000), under the
SIL Open Font License like the other Google faces in fonts/. Same
release as the SemiBold, Bold and ExtraBold beside it: the Bold in
that same download is byte for byte the Montserrat-Bold.ttf already
in fonts/, so the four cuts are one family and not four vintages of
it.
Declared by its full name (name ID 4), 'Montserrat Regular', for the
reason montserrat-bold.json gives at length. This file's name ID 1
is plain 'Montserrat' - the Regular is the one cut the family name
belongs to most of all - and it is also the name every other weight
of Montserrat answers to. Declared as 'Montserrat', it would be one
family name shared with whatever weights a machine has installed,
and fontguard, which keys its check by family, could not tell this
file from the Bold.
Weight 400, the file's own usWeightClass. A static cut rather than an
instance read out of the variable font - there is no fvar table - so
asking for 400 asks for exactly these outlines.
It has a real lower case, which on noisy-dish is never seen: the
preset uppercases every caption under the Snapchat heading (see
`uppercase` in presets/snapchat-caption.json), so a picked word is
in Montserrat's capitals like the Bebas around it.
_comment_css: Not declared in styles.css. This face arrived with a channel and is
registered from this JSON at load time (see registerFace in
js/channels.js), which is the route content/README.md describes -
nothing has to be added to the stylesheet for it.
_comment_local: What the machine may already know the face by, tried after the file
and used by the installer as the name it registers this face under
The full name first, then the PostScript name, the order the other
three Montserrat packs use. Both name this one cut. 'Montserrat' on
its own is deliberately absent: it is the name every weight of the
family answers to, and a designer's PC with the family installed
could hand back the Bold under it - a picked word heavier than the
block, which is the opposite of what this face is for.
_comment_stack: Damage limitation, never a design choice - a block laid out against
the wrong metrics is broken rather than merely different, which is
what fontguard exists to catch before anything is drawn.
The same entries as the other Montserrat packs, reached at 400. This
is the HIGHLIGHT face on a channel set in Bebas Neue Cyrillic (see
noisy-dish), which is the job poppins-regular.json does on
conspiracy-central, and it falls through ordinary-width sans faces
for the same reason: never through Anton or Impact, because a
substitute in the block's condensed register would take away the
one thing that sets a picked word apart.
